title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation primitives: the eval harness, prompt set curation and benchmarking, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidelines, and a regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, model on-call, and product owners who ship LLM features.

Scope: The document covers standards, required artifacts, runbook steps for onboarding and regression incidents, and representative examples (CLI/JSON/YAML) to ensure reproducible quality and repeatable triage.

Owners and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (engineering)
- Secondary owners: Runtime Performance team, Applied ML Evals team
- On-call (model regressions): applied-ml-oncall@redwood.ai
- Reviewers: see metadata

Principles

1. Reproducibility: every evaluation must be executable from stored artifacts (prompt sets, seed, model config, quantization profile).
2. Signal-first: prioritize prompt sets and metrics that map to customer impact (latency, hallucination rate, instruction-following).
3. Guardrails as code: quality checks and thresholds must be codified in CI and in model serving config.
4. Fast feedback and clear escalation: triage workflows should return actionable fixes within the first 24 hours for production regressions.

1) Eval Harness: Standards and Required Artifacts

Required artifacts for any eval run:
- prompt-set (JSONL) with labeled attributes (intent, difficulty, criticality)
- reference/expected outputs (where applicable) and evaluation recipes (scoring code)
- model-config snapshot (model name/version, tokenizer, weights checksum)
- runtime-config (sequence length, sampling params, batch settings)
- quantization-profile (if quantized)
- run metadata (git commit, harness version, date, agent)

Minimum harness functionality:
- deterministic, containerized execution (Docker image tag + tests)
- metric aggregation by tag (e.g., intent, length, criticality)
- support for multiple metrics: exact-match, semantic-similarity (embedding-based), factuality checks, toxicity filters, latency percentiles, token usage
- CI gating hooks: produce a machine readable artifact and a human-readable summary

Example CLI (eval-harness)

1. Run an eval locally:

$ docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace redwood/eval-harness:2026-11-01 \n  --prompts /workspace/prompt-set.jsonl \n  --model-config /workspace/model-config.json \n  --output /workspace/results/report.json

2. CI step (example YAML snippet):

steps:
  - name: run-evals
    image: redwood/eval-harness:2026-11-01
    commands:
      - /opt/eval-harness/run --prompts prompts/prod-critical.jsonl --model-config model-config.json --out results.json
      - cat results.json | jq '.summary'  # fail build if thresholds not met

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarking

Prompt set lifecycle: create -> review -> tag -> publish -> monitor.

Curation guidance:
- Tag each prompt with: intent, expected output type (completion/QA/structured), difficulty (easy/medium/hard), real-customer-example boolean, and privacy flag.
- Include at least 200 examples for any critical intent used in production features. For lower-risk features, 50-100 examples are acceptable.
- Balance: 60% natural user examples, 30% adversarial examples (edge cases), 10% synthetic stress tests.

Benchmarking metrics (recommended):
- Accuracy/Exact-match for retrieval/QA tasks
- BLEU/ROUGE when applicable
- Embedding-similarity AUC for reranking tasks
- Factuality score (external knowledge-backed checks)
- Hallucination rate (% assertions not verifiable)
- Latency p50/p90/p99 and cost-per-request

Publishing checklist:
1. Prompt set reviewed by at least one product owner and one applied-ML engineer.
2. Prompts anonymized (PII removed) and privacy flag checked.
3. Stored in canonical S3 path: s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/{name}/{version}/
4. Add prompt-set metadata JSON and link into eval harness CI job.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (High-level)

Goal: ensure a model variant is production-ready for a given workload.

Pre-onboarding (artifact collection):
- Model binary + checksum
- Training and tokenizer metadata
- Supported sequence lengths and known limitations
- Initial quantization profile (if applicable)
- Evaluation artifact: results for canonical prompt sets with thresholded metrics

Onboarding steps:
1. Run full eval-harness across canonical prompt sets (smoke + critical intents).
2. Collect perf data: latency p50/p90/p99 on target infrastructure, memory usage, GPU utilization.
3. Verify guardrails: hallucination < threshold, toxicity < threshold, accuracy >= SLAs.
4. Stage to Dedicated environment with traffic shadowing for 48-72 hours.
5. Canary to 1-5% traffic with rollback plan.

Rollout decision matrix (simplified):
- Accept: all critical metrics pass and no regressions vs baseline.
- Accept-with-guardrails: functional with mitigations (e.g., stricter timeout, fallback to safer model).
- Reject: fails critical metrics or introduces >5% customer-facing errors.

4) Quality Guardrails (implementation details)

Guardrails are implemented at two layers: evaluation-time and runtime.

Evaluation-time guardrails:
- Thresholds defined per prompt-tag and intent in a guardrails YAML. Example key fields: metric, threshold, severity, action.

Example guardrails.yaml format (text):

- intent: "invoice-extraction"
  metric: "exact_match"
  threshold: "0.92"
  severity: "critical"
  action: "block-deploy"

Runtime guardrails (serving layer):
- Response-level checks: safety filter, hallucination detector, contradiction detector, structured-output validator.
- Circuit breakers: if model p99 latency > target or safety checks fail above rate, auto-fallback to safe-model-v1 and create incident.
- Per-customer policies: ability to tighten thresholds for enterprise customers (config in customer profile).

5) Quantization Profiles and Guidelines

Purpose: guide safe quantization that preserves quality while reducing cost.

Profile artifact must include:
- quantization-type (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, GPTQ), framework and version (bitsandbytes 0.39), toolchain commands, calibration dataset reference (S3 path), observed delta metrics vs fp16 baseline.

Recommended process:
1. Select calibration dataset drawn from production prompt tags (N>=2k examples covering critical intents).
2. Run quantization recipe and evaluate against canonical prompt sets. Record delta for each metric and length bucket.
3. If any critical intent drops more than 2.5% absolute accuracy or hallucination increases more than 1.5% absolute, mark profile as non-production.
4. For approved profiles, attach 'safe-quant' tag and require runtime A/B testing with 1-5% traffic shadowing for 72 hours.

Quantization profile summary table (example text):
| profile_name | method | baseline_delta_accuracy | hallucination_delta | recommended_use |
| safe-8bit-v1 | 8-bit GPTQ | -0.8% | +0.2% | low-latency non-critical |
| perf-4bit-v2 | 4-bit PTQ | -2.1% | +0.9% | cost-sensitive but monitored |

6) Regression Triage Playbook

When a regression is detected (alert or high-level customer report):

Immediate actions (first 60 minutes):
1. Acknowledge alert and notify on-call (applied-ml-oncall).
2. Run quick diff: compare latest passing evaluation artifact vs current (diff metrics by prompt-tag).
3. Switch traffic to baseline model or enable pre-configured fallback policy if customer-facing errors > threshold.
4. Create incident in PagerDuty + Confluence incident page template.

Triage (first 24 hours):
1. Identify the scope: affected models, prompt-tags, customers, regions.
2. Search recent changes: model versions, quantization profiles, runtime kernel changes, infra changes (GPU drivers), prompt-set updates, and configuration rollouts.
3. Re-run targeted evals on suspicious vectors (use the eval-harness with the failing prompt-tags, low-cost smoke suite).
4. Produce triage summary: root-cause hypotheses and candidate mitigations (rollback, guardrail tighten, patch).
5. Implement mitigation (rollback or config change) and validate.

Postmortem and Prevention

- Postmortem must be filed within 7 days with owner, timeline, root cause, action items, and follow-up audits.
- Action items examples: add prompt tags to canonical suites, add new unit tests in eval harness, improve CI gating thresholds, update quantization profile vetting.

Metrics, Dashboards, and Alerts

Essential dashboards:
- Canonical eval dashboard: historical metric trends per prompt-tag and per model-version
- Production quality dashboard: hallucination rate, safety-filter triggers, error rate by intent, latency percentiles by model and region
- Quantization comparison dashboard: delta vs baseline across lengths and intents

Alerts (examples):
- Hallucination rate > 2x baseline for critical intent -> P1
- Accuracy drop > 5% absolute on critical prompt-set -> P1
- p99 latency breach above SLO for 10+ mins -> P2

Appendices

A. Example model-config.json (text)

{
  "model_name": "redwood-gptx-3b",
  "version": "2026-10-25",
  "tokenizer": "rwd-tokenizer-v2",
  "max_seq": "4096",
  "quantization_profile": "safe-8bit-v1"
}

B. Canonical prompt tags list (short)
- billing: invoice-extraction, charge-dispute
- search: query-refinement, reranking
- assistant: general-chat, instruction-following
- content-moderation: toxicity-detection

C. Quick links (internal)
- Eval harness repo: https://git.internal.redwood.ai/eval-harness
- Prompt sets S3: s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/
- Quant profiles bucket: s3://redwood-evals/quant-profiles/

Revision history: maintain a changelog inside the repo and update this page when guardrails, thresholds, or canonical prompt sets change.

End of document.
